They nevertheless agreed that reduction in the dosage of metronidazole is required only when hepatic function is very poor, particularly when renal function is impaired. A study in 10 severely ill patients with or without impaired hepatic and/or renal function5 also suggested that hepatic function is a very important determinant of metroni- dazole elimination. 1. J Antimicrob Chemother 1984; 14: 275–83. Infants and children. A single intravenous dose of 15 mg/kg has been suggested for neonates1 which would produce thera- peutic concentrations of metronidazole for around 24 hours in term neonates and 48 hours in preterm neonates. Renal and he- patic function is incompletely developed in newborn infants and consequently the elimination half-life of metronidazole is pro- longed and has been reported to range from 25 to 109 hours.1 Elimination half-life is inversely proportional to gestational age1,2 and as the infant matures half-life is reduced to values clos- er to those in adults.1,3 1. Pharmacokinetic studies have indicated that doses of metronidazole need not be altered in patients with renal impairment,1 although adjustments might be required in patients undergoing haemodialysis, since metronidazole and its hydroxy metabolite are efficiently cleared and extensively re- moved in such patients.2 However, in another study3 the amount of metronidazole and its hydroxy metabolite cleared was found to depend on the type of dialysis membrane used;
